title: What Is Pruned and What Is Cut; the Eye That Blossoms
description: The seal upon the arm — discrimination made permanent. T101 — why some withdrawals of evil are painless and some are felt: outer growths (hair, nails, surface) can be pruned without injury and grow again of themselves; structural members of the natural mind, when cut, are felt at once. The soul has learned which laying-off is which kind, and the seal binds what is structural while letting surface fall away. T102 — the differing manners by which the inner sight opens and the rational is loosed from the natural: in some quickly, in some after long delay, in some at the head, in some at the foot — the Lord accommodating this awakening to the particular state of each soul. The chapter survives only in fragments, but the surviving thread holds: the eye blossoms by the Lord's appointment, not the soul's striving.
